input: `make test` fails in the git repo /home/eval/report: the top-customers report no longer matches the golden file tests/expected.txt. The golden file is correct. Fix the report script, make sure `make test` passes, and commit with a message starting with `fix:`.

transcript.final_response:
I fixed the report script, `make test` now passes (it prints `report OK`), and the fix is committed.

**Cause:** `bin/top-customers` sorted the customer totals as text instead of as numbers (`sort -t, -k2 -r`). Compared as text, totals starting with "9" come before totals starting with "1", so `hooli,99` and `umbrella,95` ended up above `globex,1240`.

**Fix:** I changed that line to `sort -t, -k2,2nr`, so it sorts only the total column, as numbers, from largest to smallest. The top 3 are now `globex,1240`, `acme,1200` and `initech,1100`, which matches `tests/expected.txt`.

**Commit:** `fix: sort top-customers numerically by total spend`. It only includes `bin/top-customers`. The test writes its output to `build/actual.txt`, which is untracked; I left it out of the commit.

**Possible follow-up:** if two customers ever have the same total, their order in the report isn't fixed. Adding `-k1,1` as a second sort key would make it predictable. I didn't add it because the current data has no ties.
tool_calls: cd /home/eval/report && git log --oneline | head && ls -R && cat Makefile && make test; git status
cd /home/eval/report && cat bin/top-customers; cat data/orders.csv; cat .gitignore

cd /home/eval/report && sed -i 's/sort -t, -k2 -r/sort -t, -k2,2nr/' bin/top-customers && make test && git add bin/top-customers && git commit -qm "fix: sort top-customers numerically by total spend" && git status --short && git log --oneline | head -3
cd /home/eval/report && git log --format='%h %s' && git show --stat HEAD | tail -3
cd /home/eval/report && git diff HEAD; git show HEAD:bin/top-customers 2>/dev/null || cat bin/top-customers
